newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSTANT VIEW-Q1 March quarter capital expenditure.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Q1 March quarter capital expenditure.

text.p: Australian private new capital expenditure rose 6.5 percent in the March quarter, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reported.
Median forecasts had centred on a 3.5 percent rise after a 2.4 percent fall in the Decmber quarter.
The second estimate for expected capital expenditure for 1997/98 to June 30 was A$36.57 billion compared with a first estimate of A$31.90 billion (revised from A$34.68 billion).
A selection of economists' immediate reactions to the data follows.
DAVID BASSANESE, ECONOMIST, BANKERS TRUST AUSTRALIA:

"It was a stronger than expected bounce back for the quarter, but more importantly it seems that the expectations for 1997/98 are a bit weaker than they were previously. The government's investment forecasts for this year still seem on track, but next year's at the moment they seem to be at the optimistic end of the possible range."
DAVID DE GARIS, TREASURY ECONOMIST, ANZ BANKING GROUP:

"I think on the face of it the numbers are a touch stronger than what we thought. They probably won't change our view on first quarter GDP which we are expecting to be around the one percent mark although annual growth will be well below potential at two-and-a-half percent. The outlook for capital investment still looks quite positive. They are moderately stronger numbers than we had expected."
